patients.label: 32-year-old primigravida with obstetric renal cortical necrosis after massive postpartum hemorrhage
attribution_limitations: The case narrative says hypertension developed following the cesarean section, whereas the discussion says the case presented with proteinuria and hypertension before delivery.

The case narrative says dialysis was discontinued 6 months after discharge, whereas the discussion says PD was discontinued about 6 months post-onset; the abstract says renal function improved over 6 months allowing discontinuation.

Pre-eclampsia is a suspicion at 39 weeks gestation in the case text (provisional, p1-f008), a listed pregnancy disorder of the present case in Table 2 (p1-f009) and an authors suggestion of onset preceding RCN in the discussion (p1-f010).

The text says only treatment for metabolic acidosis and renal anemia; the agents appear only on the Figure 4 treatment bars (Sodium Bicarbonate 3000 mg, DPA 30 – 120 μg/month, Daprodustat 2 – 4 mg), with DPA expanded as darbepoetin α in the caption.
Table 1 prints ADAMTS13 activity as 77 with unit % but the normal range as > 0.78.
The descriptor Mongolian is given for the patient without saying whether it denotes nationality or ethnicity.
The authors speculate that glomerular endothelial injury from pre-eclampsia and DIC aggravated RCN severity and that biopsy timing may have altered the histology.

Two pathology statements contain the word normal without calling a result normal: outer cortex tubules showed loss of normal cytologic features, and deeper cortex glomeruli largely maintained a normal morphology while ischemic changes were observed in that region.
